ai.description: This 60–90 cm snake features a dark olive-brown body with a bright red or orange belly. It is distinguished by a prominent yellow lateral stripe and strongly keeled scales.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Painted Keelback is best identified by the distinct, bright reddish-orange coloration on its belly, which contrasts sharply with its dark, olive-brown dorsal scales.
ai.habitat: The Painted Keelback inhabits freshwater wetlands, marshes, and rice paddies in the lowlands of the Indian subcontinent, typically favoring areas with dense aquatic vegetation.
ai.behavior: The Painted Keelback is a highly aquatic snake that primarily hunts for fish and frogs in shallow, vegetated wetlands during the day.
ai.reproductionNotes: The Painted Keelback is ovoviviparous, giving birth to live young. They breed during the monsoon season, typically producing litters of 6–12 offspring.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Painted Keelback is found across the Gangetic plains and northeastern India, typically inhabiting low-elevation wetlands, marshes, and rice paddies.
